role: TNT in the whole-server replay: BlockTNT's flint-and-steel activation (primed entity spawn, block to air, lighter wear) and the primed TNT's explode as a 4.0 newExplosion over the replay's item pool, living entities and the server player, with the S27 knockback accumulated for the player.

structs.name: tnt_blast
structs.java: Explosion's context for one TNT blast: the exploder's placer and the player's knockback entry in Explosion.field_77288_k

gpu: its former globals, function statics and lazily built tables are gone (lane/gpuenv, L2): per-environment state lives in struct env (csrc/engine/env.h), per-dimension state in the replay's dims, constant tables are built before main; csrc/tests/globals.sh lists what is left
lines 133-134 and 140-141, function tnt_replay_explode: writes the global explosion flags expl_exclude_ie and expl_placed_by_player around the call
function blast_query: the query list holds every match (AN_QUERY_LIST, AN_MAX_ENTITIES from the env scratch stack) (lane/querybounds, AI-02)
lines 80-121, function blast_query: the blast's entity pass is a callback table (expl_extra.attack_from / add_motion function pointers over void* entities)
notes: Called from survival.c (tnt_server_activate on block 46 when not sneaking) and serverreplay.c (installs tnt_replay_explode as iew.on_tnt_explode). No blast protection is modelled, so the player's knockback vector is the push itself. The primed entity's fuse and motion are item_entity.c's IE_TNT; fire priming is fire.c. Tests listed are those that link serverreplay; which recordings exercise TNT was not verified. The Explosion.java member names are the vanilla ones expl_run_extras stands in for, not checked in explosion.c.
